newsitem.title: USA: CBOT grains, soy complex open lower on setback.
newsitem.headline: CBOT grains, soy complex open lower on setback.

text.p: A setback amid signals the markets were overbought pressed CBOT grain and soy complex futures lower on the open, traders said.
Wheat, soybean and corn futures have been rallying for roughly a week on bullish input from Friday's bullish USDA production, stocks and winter wheat seedings report.
"It's really overdone (overbought) and due to correct," a trader said.
Soy complex and corn futures were underpinned by a bullish USDA weekly export sales report plus uncertainty about South American weather patterns were supportive.
But there was a private forecast for improved chances for rain in South America by the weekend, they said.
Wheat was pressured by USDA's weekly export sales report and on news Algeria and Yemen bought wheat from sources other than the U.S.
At 0942 CST, soybeans were 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 1/4 higher, with January down 1/2 at $7.44. Soyoil was 0.06 to 0.15 cent per lb lower and soymeal was $0.50 per ton higher to $0.50 lower.
Wheat was 1-1/4 to two cents per bushel lower, with March down 1-3/4 at $3.88-1/2. Corn was 1/4 cent a bushel lower to 1/2 higher, with March down 1/4 at $2.73-1/2.
